label: At D1, low after a rewarded trial, higher after reaching S1; unrewarded level holds late in episode.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (state - action) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == prev_action)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 31 (always on, mean 0.70). Beyond the timing baseline, which falls late in the episode, it is driven mostly at D1 by the previous trial outcome shown then: it drops by about 0.17 after a rewarded trial and is higher (+0.15) when the previous trial reached S1 than S2 (so S2-rewarded is lowest and S1-unrewarded highest). After unrewarded trials it does not follow the late-episode decline of the baseline (the prev_reward==0 x ep_trial term, positive), so the gap between rewarded and unrewarded grows late in the episode. GO and D2 effects are small: GO is slightly lower after reward, and at D2 it is higher after a1->S2 and lower after a2->S1 (rare transitions, the state - action term). The free fit adds these GO/D2 terms, a common-transition bump at D1, and episode-time scaling of the S1 effect (dev 0.81 vs 0.69 for the short form). The observer belief adds little once the last trial is in. No future variables used.

issues: The claim that the unrewarded level holds late in the episode is false. The (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==0)*ep_trial term only works as a stand-in for 'the previous trial is known' (D1 steps where prev is '?' get 0). Add a plain (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==0) indicator and the ep_trial weight drops to +0.000: r1 / r0 / S1 scores test 0.733, higher than the recorded 0.693. With (phase==D1)*(prev_reward>=0) in place, the r0*ep_trial weight is also 0.000 (test 0.610). So the gap between rewarded and unrewarded trials does not widen late in the episode.
Supporting check: (D1)*(prev_reward==1)*ep_trial adds nothing (0.579 vs 0.579 without it), so the episode-time story has no other support either.

The short form leaves out the D2 rare-transition effect (state - action, weight +0.106: higher after a1->S2, lower after a2->S1). Adding it is worth about +0.08 test (0.693 -> 0.775 as a 4-term fit), and it accounts for much of the gap to the free fit's 0.818.

Misses on the recorded short form: the worst windows are late-episode D1 steps after unrewarded trials, over-predicted by about 0.19 (actual ~0.57 vs predicted ~0.76). The linear ep_trial term overshoots there, which is again a sign it is a fitted correction.

Small systematic error left in every form: a previous a2 choice is over-predicted at D1 by about 0.05-0.08 (after a2 S1 r/u and a2 S2 r). Adding prev_action as a separate 4th term gives no test gain, so I did not add it.
The residual tables do confirm the reward drop (about -0.17) and the S1-over-S2 raise (about +0.14) at D1.
skeptic.revised_label: At D1: low after rewarded trials, higher after reaching S1; at D2: higher after a1->S2, lower after a2->S1.

final_label: At D1: low after rewarded trials, higher after reaching S1; at D2: higher after a1->S2, lower after a2->S1.
